issues.evidence: The Tibetan "ཆོས་གང་སྤྱོད་པ་དེ་ཡང་དམིགས་པར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ" says the phenomena practiced do not become objects of apprehension (negation "མི་འགྱུར"). Khenrab (bo-khenrab 1-11): "འཁོར་གསུམ་མི་དམིགས་པ་སྤྱད་པ" (practice of non-apprehension of the three spheres). The English drops the negation and says the opposite.
issues.fix: Whatever phenomena they practice are also not apprehended

issues.span: Will become afraid upon hearing the Mother of the Victors.
issues.evidence: The Tibetan "ཐོས་སྐྲག་པར་ཡོང་མི་འགྱུར" means they will never become afraid. Mipham (bo-mipham 1-14): "སྐྲག་པར་ཡོངས་ཡེ་མི་འགྱུར་པར"; Rangjung (bo-rangjung 1-14): "སྐྲག་པ་ཡོངས་སུ་མེད་པར་གྱུར་ཏེ". Sanskrit "trāso na bheṣyati". The English reverses the sense.
issues.fix: Will never become afraid upon hearing the Mother of the Victors.

issues.evidence: Locked term "གང་ཟག་དམ་པ" = "holy being"; the English uses "noble beings", which is not the locked rendering and suggests "ārya".
issues.fix: This is the supreme armor of holy beings.

issues.evidence: The Tibetan "བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མཁས་རིག་གང་གི་དུས་ཀྱི་ཚེ ... སྐྱེ་མེད་རྣམ་པར་བསམས་ཏེ་འདི་ལྟར་སྤྱོད་བྱེད་ཅིང" says only "whenever/at the time when" the bodhisattva contemplates the unborn and practices thus. Nothing in the Tibetan, Sanskrit ("yasmiṃś ca kāli samaye") or the commentaries (bo-mipham 1-23, bo-rangjung 1-23) speaks of countless eons.
issues.fix: Contemplates the unborn and practices in this way,

issues.span: This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
issues.evidence: The final line "འདི་ནི་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་མཆོག་སྤྱོད་མ་ཡིན" ends in "མ་ཡིན" (is not). Sanskrit "na ca eṣā ... caryā"; Mipham (bo-mipham 1-24): "སྤྱོད་པ་མ་ཡིན"; Rangjung (bo-rangjung 1-24): "སྤྱོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ". The English asserts the opposite.
issues.fix: This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.

issues.span: And whoever abides in consciousness, abides in the true nature of phenomena;
issues.evidence: The Tibetan "རྣམ་ཤེས་གང་མི་གནས་པ་ཆོས་ཉིད་གནས་པ་སྟེ" has "མི་གནས" (does not abide): whoever does not abide in consciousness abides in the true nature. Mipham (bo-mipham 2-1): "རྣམ་ཤེས་གང་ལ་མི་གནས་པ། དེ་ནི ... ཆོས་ཉིད ... ལ་གནས་པ". The English drops the negation.
issues.fix: And whoever does not abide in consciousness abides in the true nature of phenomena;

issues.span: Whoever trains in training and non-training, that is training.
issues.evidence: The Tibetan "གང་ཞིག་སློབ་མི་སློབ་ལ་མི་སློབ་དེ་སློབ་ཡིན" has "མི་སློབ" after "ལ": whoever does not train in training and non-training, that is (true) training. Mipham (bo-mipham 2-7): "སློབ་པ ... མི་སློབ་པ ... ཆོས་གང་ལའང་མི་སློབ་པ་དེ་ནི་ཡང་དག་པའི་ལམ་ལ་སློབ་པ་ཡིན"; Rangjung (bo-rangjung 2-7): "སློབ་པ་དང་མི་སློབ་པའི་ས་ལ་མི་སློབ་པ་དེ་ནི ... སློབ་པ་ཡིན". The English drops the negation.
issues.fix: Whoever does not train in training and non-training, that is training.

issues.evidence: Locked term "ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན" = "perfection of wisdom"; line 1 "ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་མཆོག" is rendered "supreme transcendent insight" though line 4 uses the locked rendering.
issues.fix: Likewise, through the qualities of the supreme perfection of wisdom,

issues.evidence: Line 2 "ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་འདིར་སྤྱོད་པ་མཁས་པ་སོམ་ཉི་མེད" says the bodhisattva is skilled in practicing this perfection and has no doubt ("སོམ་ཉི་མེད"). Sanskrit "na ca kāṅkṣati"; Mipham (bo-mipham 2-51): "སོམས་ཉི་མེད་པར་གྱུར་ནས"; Rangjung (bo-rangjung 2-51): "རྟོགས་པ་ལ་སོམ་ཉི་མེད". The English omits "without doubt".
issues.fix: Skillfully practiced this perfection, without doubt,

issues.evidence: Tibetan "ལྷ་རྒྱལ་བརྒྱ་བྱིན" is Śakra (locked: "Śakra, king of the gods"); Sanskrit "śakro ... devarājo"; Rangjung (bo-rangjung 4-1): "ལྷའི་དབང་པོ་བརྒྱ་བྱིན". The English names a different deity, Brahmā.

issues.span: It is the armor of the aggregates, elements, and sense bases;
issues.evidence: The Tibetan "ཕུང་པོ་ཁམས་དང་སྐྱེ་མཆེད་རྣམས་ཀྱི་གོ་ཆ་མིན" ends in "མིན" (is not). Sanskrit "na ca skandhadhātu na ca āyatanaiḥ sanaddhāḥ"; Mipham (bo-mipham 4-46): "གོ་ཆ་བགོ་བ་མིན"; Khenrab (bo-khenrab 4-46): "གོ་ཆ་དགོ་བ་མིན". The English drops the negation.
issues.fix: It is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, and sense bases;

issues.span: And rely on other śramaṇas and brahmins;
issues.evidence: The Tibetan "དགེ་སྦྱོང་དག་དང་བྲམ་ཟེ་གཞན་ལ་རྟེན་མི་བྱེད" has "མི་བྱེད" (do not rely). Sanskrit "na ca anya te śramaṇa brāhmaṇa āśrayanti"; Mipham (bo-mipham 4-57): "རྟེན་པར་མི་བྱེད"; Rangjung (bo-rangjung 4-57): "བརྟེན་པ་མི་བྱེད". The English asserts the opposite.
issues.fix: And do not rely on other śramaṇas and brahmins;

issues.span: And by the final contact with the flame, the wick is consumed,
issues.evidence: The Tibetan "མེ་ལྕེ་ཕྲད་པ་ཐམས་སྙིང་པོ་ཚིག་མིན་ལ" says the (last) contact does not consume it ("ཚིག་མིན"). Mipham (bo-mipham 4-71): "མེ་ལྕེ་ཕྲད་པ་ཐ་མ་ཁོ་ནས་ཀྱང་མར་གྱི་སྙིང་པོ་དེ་ཚིག་པ་མིན"; Khenrab (bo-khenrab 4-71) the same; Sanskrit "na hi arci paścimanipāta ... dagdhā". The English reverses it, contradicting the next line.
issues.fix: And by the final contact with the flame, the wick is not consumed,

issues.span: their host of servants and friends
issues.evidence: Tibetan "གཉེན་བཤེས་ཚོགས" means kin and friends; Sanskrit "jātisaṅgho" (kin group); Khenrab (bo-khenrab 4-92) "རང་གི་གཉེན་རྣམས ... གཉེན་བཤེས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས". Nothing in the Tibetan mentions servants.
issues.fix: their host of kin and friends

issues.span:
does not live happily all alone
While leaving
issues.evidence: The Tibetan says the caravan leader alone lives happily and does not leave his kin and friends unhappy (Mipham, bo-mipham 4-92: "རང་ཉིད་འབའ་ཞིག ... བདེ་བར་འཚོ་བར་བྱེད་ཅིང ... ཡིད་མི་བདེ་བར་འཇོག་པར་བྱེད་པ་མིན"). The English negation can be read as denying that he lives happily.
issues.fix: The merchant alone lives happily, yet does not leave his host of kin and friends unhappy.

issues.evidence: The Tibetan "བདག་ལུང་བསྟན་སྙམ་རློམ་སེམས" is the thought "I have been prophesied" (locked: "ལུང་བསྟན"=prophecy). Mipham (bo-mipham 5-4): "བདག་ལུང་བསྟན་པ་ཉིད་དུ་གྱུར་པའོ་སྙམ"; Sanskrit "vyākṛto 'smi". "Vision" has no basis.
The Tibetan "དཔག་ཚད་ལྔ་བརྒྱ" is five hundred yojanas. Sanskrit "pañcayojanaśate"; Mipham (bo-mipham 5-9): "དཔག་ཚད་ལྔ་བརྒྱ"; Rangjung (bo-rangjung 5-9): "དཔག་ཚད་ལྔ་བརྒྱ་ཡོད་པའི་རི་སུལ".

issues.span:
Whoever, in a mountain cleft of fifty yojanas,
Filled with snakes, abides for many tens of millions of years,
That bodhisattva
issues.evidence: The Tibetan "གནས་བྱེད་ཀྱང་" is concessive (even though one abides there ...), then "that bodhisattva who does not know this solitude". The English leaves "Whoever ... abides" without a main clause and loses "even though".
issues.fix: Even if one abides for many tens of millions of years in a mountain cleft of five hundred yojanas filled with snakes, that bodhisattva who does not know this solitude

issues.evidence: The Tibetan "རྣལ་འབྱོར་དོར་མི་བྱ" means one should not abandon the yoga. Sanskrit "yogu na riñcitavyo"; Rangjung (bo-rangjung 5-23, same passage) and Mipham support persevering. The English drops the negation.
